Understanding pedagogical challenges faced by technology teachers in special needs classrooms
abstract: <jats:p>Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.</jats:p>

Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
abstract:
<jats:p>Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored.
Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes.
Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement.
Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization.
Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.</jats:p>

title: A Review of Phishing Detection Techniques Using Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
abstract: <jats:p>The goal of phishing attacks, which rank high among cyber risks, is to steal sensitive information (such as login passwords, financial data, and more) from unsuspecting people and companies. Blacklist, whitelist, rule, heuristic, and signature-based detection methods are no longer suitable due to the rising sophistication of phishing schemes. As a result, ML, DL, and NLP are rapidly becoming into effective instruments for detecting both well-known and brand-new forms of phishing. Background on phishing assaults, old ways of detecting them, and recent advances in intelligent phishing detection are all included in this article. It delves into several machine learning algorithms such as decision tree, LSTM, ANN, CNN, and RNN, as well as deep learning models like KNN, NB, and SVM. Also, natural language processing methods including word embedding, sentiment analysis, text categorization, and tokenization are explored with the aim of detecting phishing material. Presenting a comprehensive, precise, and up-to-the-minute phishing detection system is the ultimate goal of this study, which focuses on machine learning frameworks, performance indicators, present obstacles, and future research directions.</jats:p>

Cyber Defense Digital Twins: A Federated Learning and Zero-Trust AI Architecture for Autonomous Threat Prediction and Response
abstract: <jats:p>Modern enterprise networks operate under persistent threats that exploit cloud-native misconfigurations, identity sprawl, and API vulnerabilities at machine speed. Existing security operations center (SOC) architectures remain largely reactive, signature-dependent, and incapable of predicting multi-stage lateral movement. This paper proposes the Cognitive Cyber Defense Digital Twin (CCDT), a unified architecture integrating federated learning (FL), graph neural network (GNN)-based attack-path forecasting, adversarially hardened detection models, and autonomous Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) with deception engineering. The CCDT constructs a continuously synchronized digital replica of organizational assets and employs reinforcement learning-based red agents to stress-test detection models. A federated intelligence mesh enables cross-organizational privacy-preserving gradient sharing. Experimental evaluations against CICIDS-2018 and LANL datasets demonstrate 52% faster attack-path detection, 41% reduction in false positive rate, and 60% reduction in mean-time-to-respond (MTTR) compared to traditional SOC baselines. Integrated Explainable AI (XAI) modules using SHAP values enable audit-ready compliance reporting. The CCDT represents a paradigm shift from reactive monitoring to predictive, autonomous, and privacy-preserving cyber defense for hybrid cloud environments.</jats:p>

title: Transforming Education through Technology: The Case of COVID 19 Digital Learning in Nagaland
abstract:
<jats:p>Through the perspective of the COVID-19 pandemic and the disruption and opportunity it engendered, this chapter follows a transformative effect of EdTech and Digital education in India particularly in Nagaland through analysis. Drawing upon national policy frameworks, conceptual literature on educational technology, and contextual evidence based on the case of Nagaland, the chapter considers the rapid migration to digital learning as an emergency strategy (in response to the ongoing institution closures) based on the stark shifts in pedagogical practice, access to education services, and preparedness. The findings show that, including the ability of national programmes such as NEP 2020, SWAYAM, DIKSHA, PM e-VIDYA, and others, to promote access to digital tools was low within periphery or hill areas (e.g., Nagaland), due to lack of infrastructural resources, digital divide, unprepared teachers and economic/social divides, and more. The pandemic exposed the deep social and infrastructure divides in connectivity, device availability, assessment and learner engagement, with implications that were especially grave in rural and tribal settings. Although it accelerated the pace of innovation and the application of blended and low-tech learning practices teachers have been experimenting with digital platforms and the post-COVID recovery process, including remedial programmes and hybrid instruction. The chapter also discusses that blended learning is the most fitting, viable and sustainable approach for reaching the technological level in the field of educational technology at Nagaland. It implies that technology-mediated education can improve equity, quality, and resilience, but only under the conditions of inclusive policy design, strong digital infrastructure, vigorous teacher capability building, and culturally appropriate digital content.
Keywords: Educational technology, digital learning, COVID-19, Nagaland, online education, Challenges, blended learning</jats:p>

title: Integrating Natural Language Processing in Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services Research Using Normalization Process Theory: Implementation Report.
abstract: Anxiety problems are prevalent among autistic children and adolescents and those with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Natural language processing (NLP) is increasingly used to structure information from electronic health records (EHRs), but its implementation within secure child and adolescent mental health services (CAMHS) research environments is less frequently reported. This study documented the specification, governance, integration, and evaluation of an NLP-enabled information extraction workflow within the Oxford Health National Health Service (NHS) Foundation Trust CAMHS research setting for extracting documented anxiety treatment information and outcome-related text from the EHRs of autistic young people and those with ADHD and examined implementation using normalization process theory (NPT). A multidisciplinary team developed a locally deployed NLP pipeline to identify labeled text spans describing presenting problems, medication attributes, psychological therapies, and treatment outcomes in pseudonymized EHR notes. Implementation followed an iterative seven-phase road map: (1) defining research questions, (2) identifying key constructs, (3) codeveloping an annotation schema, (4) training human annotators, (5) resolving annotation discrepancies, (6) large-scale annotation of EHR data, and (7) developing and evaluating the NLP model. NPT was applied throughout to guide implementation and evaluate progress. Quantitative outcomes (data volume processed, annotation reliability, and model performance) and qualitative feedback were collected to assess implementation success. The source cohort comprised 454,127 notes from 5906 patients; 697 (0.2%) randomly selected, manually annotated notes from 302 (5.1%) patients were used for model development and held-out evaluation. Category-specific position-based Krippendorff α values ranged from 0.325 to 0.579 for problem, psychological therapy, and outcome spans and from 0.665 to 0.967 for medication spans. Agreement was highest for medication names, doses, and frequencies and lowest for cognitive problems and treatment outcomes. Held-out macroaveraged F1-score was 0.87 (95% CI 0.86-0.89) across the 4 medication labels and 0.71 (95% CI 0.68-0.73) across the 5 problem labels, psychological therapy labels, and outcome labels; label-specific F1-score ranged from 0.60 to 0.98. Team-generated implementation records indicated that multidisciplinary schema development and clear protocols supported shared understanding and engagement, whereas annotation burden, documentation variability, data access delays, and computing constraints impeded implementation. No major adverse events or harms were reported. This report demonstrates the feasibility of integrating NLP tools into NHS CAMHS research workflows to extract structured information on anxiety treatments from routine clinical records. The NPT framework provided a structured approach for documenting the organizational work, barriers, and adaptations involved. External validation, refinement of less reliable labels, and further evaluation are required before broader use. RR2-10.31234/osf.io/r4gyw.

title: Early Prediction and Prognosis in Acute Kidney Injury Using a Biomarker-Aware Transformer: Retrospective Multicenter Study.
abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common, life-threatening complication among hospitalized patients. Timely prediction is crucial for prevention, while accurate prognosis following onset is essential for guiding care. Although electronic health records (EHRs) provide rich longitudinal data, their high dimensionality, heterogeneity, and temporal complexity pose challenges for traditional machine learning. The aim of this study was to develop and evaluate a transformer-based model for generalizable AKI prediction and prognosis by modeling long-range temporal dependencies and complex relationships in heterogeneous EHR data and to examine its interpretability. We developed the Biomarker-Aware Transformer for AKI (BAT-AKI), which integrates multidimensional embeddings capturing temporal dynamics, textual descriptions, hierarchical ontology structures, and semantic relationships in EHRs. To enhance sensitivity to AKI-related biomarker fluctuations, BAT-AKI combines masked language modeling with a novel biomarker abnormality-aware pretraining task. The model was pretrained and fine-tuned for 4 tasks: AKI onset, early reversal, recovery at discharge, and 90-day post-AKI mortality. Pretraining and internal validation used data from the National Patient-Centered Clinical Research Network (PCORnet) site, with external validation across 3 additional sites. BAT-AKI achieved the strongest overall discrimination, outperforming baseline models in area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) on most tasks. For AKI onset prediction, it achieved an AUROC of 0.8549 (95% CI 0.8433-0.8658) and an AUPRC of 0.6041 (95% CI 0.5786-0.6292), exceeding the second-best baseline by 2.8% in AUROC and 8.1% in AUPRC. Across prognostic tasks, BAT-AKI achieved AUROCs of 0.6006 (95% CI 0.5703-0.6318), 0.6080 (95% CI 0.5745-0.6397), and 0.8017 (95% CI 0.7708-0.8311) and AUPRCs of 0.7036 (95% CI 0.6690-0.7388), 0.7417 (95% CI 0.7082-0.7765), and 0.5063 (95% CI 0.4422-0.5684) for early reversal, recovery at discharge, and 90-day post-AKI mortality, respectively, corresponding to relative gains of 2.4% to 6% in AUROC and 3.7% to 4.1% in AUPRC over the second-best baseline. Performance remained stable across external cohorts, with AKI onset AUROCs ranging from 0.7754 (95% CI 0.7677-0.7827) to 0.7989 (95% CI 0.7885-0.8092) and AUPRCs ranging from 0.4777 (95% CI 0.4631-0.4924) to 0.5687 (95% CI 0.5495-0.5871), corresponding to relative improvements of 3.7% to 5.3% in AUROC and 16.8% to 25.3% in AUPRC over the transformer baseline. In a low-resource setting using only 2% of the fine-tuning data, BAT-AKI achieved an AUROC of 0.7898 (95% CI 0.7759-0.8036) and an AUPRC of 0.4903 (95% CI 0.4640-0.5178) for AKI onset prediction, exceeding the second-best baseline by 4.2% in AUROC and 10.9% in AUPRC. Visualization of embeddings, attention patterns, and integrated-gradient feature attributions highlighted clinically meaningful relationships and patient-specific trajectories. BAT-AKI provides generalizable AKI prediction and prognosis with consistent discrimination across institutions, while offering interpretability insights into its predictions, supporting its potential for early warning and AKI care optimization.

title: Assessment of App Quality, User Experience, and Willingness to Recommend a Digital Therapeutic for Patients With Axial Spondyloarthritis: Subanalysis of a 12-Week Pretest-Posttest Intervention Study.
abstract: Axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) is a chronic inflammatory rheumatic disease affecting the axial skeleton that requires regular physical exercise in addition to pharmacotherapy. However, a significant proportion of patients do not exercise frequently enough. Axia is a digital therapeutic (DTx) that offers a solution by providing a disease-specific and patient-tailored home-based exercise program for patients with axSpA. The app combines structured exercise with patient education and disease management features and incorporates gamification and behavioral conditioning to promote user engagement. However, it has remained unclear how Axia is perceived and evaluated by patients. This study aimed to describe app quality, user experience, and willingness to recommend the app to others after 12 weeks of use by applying standardized questionnaires. This single-center study was conducted at an outpatient tertiary clinic. After 12 weeks of ad libitum app use, 27 participants with axSpA completed paper-based assessments of the user version of the Mobile App Rating Scale (uMARS; range 1-5) and the net promoter score (NPS; range -100% to +100%). The mean overall uMARS app quality score was 4.44 (SD 0.43). Functionality received the highest mean score (4.54, SD 0.53), whereas information received the lowest (4.34, SD 0.49). The mean NPS was 9.52 (SD 0.75), corresponding to an overall NPS of 93%. The uMARS overall quality score correlated strongly with the NPS (ρ=0.57; P=.002). Except for physical therapy at baseline, no other baseline characteristic or therapeutic effect correlated with either the uMARS or NPS. Axia was perceived as a user-friendly DTx after 12 weeks of use. The findings support the acceptability of disease-specific DTx for patients with axSpA and the potential integration of DTx into routine care.

title: A Conceptual Framework for Understanding Intelligent Behavior in Fungal Mycelia.
abstract: Fungi exhibit remarkably complex behavior through their mycelial networks, which consist of thread-like structures known as hyphae. Recent research on saprotrophic fungi has demonstrated that their mycelium behaves in ways that indicate memory, learning, decision-making, and problem-solving based on spatial pattern recognition-all of which are considered intelligent features. I present a framework to study the behavior of fungal mycelia as an emergent entity from decentralized control of numerous simple reactions at the hyphal level. The framework is based on the concept of swarm intelligence, for which internal communication is the key mechanism. Consistent with Trewavas' definition, the intelligence of a mycelium is evaluated purely in terms of its behavior and does not presuppose any form of consciousness. The paper also reviews recent findings that support the potential role of electrical signal transfer across the mycelial network as the mechanism that enables fungal mycelia to engage in intelligent behavior. The fungal mycelial network therefore provides a useful model for studying intelligent behavior in non-neural organisms and its evolution from unicellular to multicellular systems.

title: AI Literacy and Training Needs Among French Midwifery Students: National Cross-Sectional Online Survey and Exploratory Qualitative Follow-Up.
abstract: AI is increasingly relevant to health care and health professional education, but AI-related knowledge, perceptions, and training needs among midwifery students remain underdocumented. Evidence is needed to inform midwifery curricula and to clarify how students understand and operationalize AI in training and placements. This cross-sectional online study aimed to assess AI-related knowledge, perceptions, perceived risks, and training needs among French midwifery students. We conducted a national cross-sectional online survey of students enrolled in years 2 to 5 of the French midwifery curriculum between January and May 2025, complemented by exploratory qualitative follow-up interviews. Of 34 midwifery schools and universities contacted, 30 confirmed dissemination of the survey link through institutional and student-association channels. The voluntary, anonymous survey combined 5 previously published instruments or questionnaires administered in linguistically validated French versions. Likert-type items were analyzed descriptively on a 1 to 5 scale at the item level and through post hoc descriptive thematic summaries across 5 domains and 23 themes. Analyses were restricted to fully completed survey entries, with no imputation, inferential testing, or subgroup comparisons. Eight volunteer students from 1 school in eastern France participated in semistructured interviews, which were analyzed thematically to provide exploratory contextual observations. Of 414 initiated survey entries, 190 (45.9%) were fully completed and analyzed. Self-reported AI knowledge and familiarity were below the scale midpoint, with the lowest score observed for familiarity with advanced AI techniques (1.20, 95% CI 1.13-1.27). General AI familiarity was higher (n=91, 47.9% agreement) than familiarity with specific concepts such as machine learning (n=20, 10.5%) or deep learning (n=13, 6.8%). Perceived ability to use AI for clinical purposes was limited (2.05, 95% CI 1.93-2.16). In contrast, students strongly endorsed AI education, particularly the belief that students and professionals should be trained in AI (4.11, 95% CI 4.02-4.20). Prior exposure to AI (1.36, 95% CI 1.27-1.45) and perceived institutional and social support (1.43, 95% CI 1.34-1.52) were low. Ethics- and safety-related concerns were salient, with the highest score for evidence and safety requirements (4.04, 95% CI 3.96-4.12). Exploratory interviews suggested that students often referred to AI through everyday generative tools, reported little supervised exposure to AI in clinical placements, and emphasized safety, privacy, accountability, and preservation of human judgment. Interpreted as a time-bound baseline, these findings suggest an AI readiness gap among French midwifery students, in which low perceived knowledge and limited clinical readiness coexist with strong demand for training and high salience of safety and governance. They support the progressive and proportionate introduction of AI literacy in midwifery education, explicitly distinguishing general AI, generative AI tools, and regulated clinical AI systems. Future work should develop and validate midwifery-specific AI literacy measures and evaluate curriculum interventions.

title: Selective Electronic Pre-Activation of OH Bonds in Extremely Confined Water.
abstract: Water under molecular-scale confinement is not simply a geometrically restricted form of bulk water, but can acquire distinct electronic, structural, and collective properties. However, how such an extremely confined state reshapes water's intrinsic chemistry remains poorly understood. Here, using ab initio calculations and enhanced-sampling machine-learning potential molecular dynamics, we show that extreme two-dimensional confinement activates water for proton generation. Monolayer-confined water exhibits a substantially lower free-energy barrier for forming separated H3O+ and OH- ions than bulk water, and this tendency is further enhanced by lateral compression and nuclear quantum fluctuations. This enhanced reactivity does not arise from a uniform weakening of all water molecules. Instead, confinement makes OH bonds breaking selectively. The water molecule contains electronically distinct OH bonds, with weak in-plane bonds preferentially activated for proton release, while stronger dangling bonds remain relatively inactive. The surrounding hydrogen-bond network then provides disordered pathways for proton relocation, and the enhanced in-plane polarization stabilizes the charged products. Our results suggest that two-dimensional confined water can act as an active and superdielectric medium as indicated by recent experiments. Our findings reveal extreme confinement as a route to tune water-mediated chemistry, with implications for nanofluidics, geochemical pores, biological environments, and catalytic interfaces.
ai_summary: Water under molecular-scale confinement is not just a geometrically restricted form of bulk water, but can acquire distinct electronic, structural, and collective properties . This enhanced reactivity does not arise from a uniform weakening of all water molecules . Instead, confinement makes OH bonds breaking selectively .

title: The Effect of Bariatric Surgery on Homocysteine Levels: A Meta-analysis.
abstract: Homocysteine is an amino acid generated during the metabolism of methionine, which is an essential amino acid. Elevated levels of homocysteine are identified as an independent risk factor for cardiovascular disease (CVD). Bariatric surgery is known to lower the risk of CVD. Therefore, this meta-analysis aimed to assess the effect of bariatric surgery on circulating homocysteine levels. A comprehensive systematic search was conducted in 4 databases. The meta-analysis utilized Comprehensive Meta-Analysis (CMA) V4 software. The overall effect size was evaluated using a random-effects model along with a leave-one-out approach. The random-effects meta-analysis of 18 studies involving 1576 participants revealed a nonsignificant increase in serum homocysteine levels post bariatric surgery (WMD: 0.319, 95% CI: -0.208 to 0.847, 95% PI: -1.862 to 2.501, P=0.235; I2=96.45%). In subanalyses, there were no significant variations in homocysteine levels based on the duration of follow-up. The findings of this study suggest that bariatric surgery does not lead to significant changes in homocysteine levels, and this conclusion remains consistent regardless of the time elapsed since the procedure.

title: FlexGlue: Sparse-to-Dense Feature Matching and Visual Disambiguation
abstract: To estimate correspondences across images, existing approaches match either sparse interest points, which is highly efficient but limited by repeatability, or dense pixel grids, which is robust but expensive. Furthermore, these approaches are trained with only matching pairs and thus often fail to reject unrelated pairs that exhibit visual symmetries, which is equally important in applications like Structure-from-Motion (SfM). We bridge these gaps by introducing FlexGlue, a neural network for asymmetric sparse-to-dense matching and disambiguation. Given two images and coordinates of points in the first image, FlexGlue estimates the coordinates of the corresponding points in the second image while simultaneously rejecting the pair if non-matching. By searching for a limited set of correspondences among dense pixels, our approach is both fast and effective at both matching and disambiguation: it combines the sub-pixel accuracy of dense matching with the speed of sparse matching, while rejecting incorrect pairs with high precision. Experiments on multiple datasets show that FlexGlue pushes the Pareto frontier in relative pose estimation and significantly outperforms existing approaches for SfM and visual localization. FlexGlue is publicly available at https://github.com/cvg/flexglue .
ai_summary: FlexGlue is a neural network for asymmetric sparse-to-dense matching and disambiguation . It combines the sub-pixel accuracy of dense matching with the speed of sparse matching, while rejecting incorrect pairs .

title: RobustRLlib: A Unified Library and Benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
abstract: Robust reinforcement learning (RL) is critical for reliable real-world deployment, where policies may fail under diverse shifts and disruptions. Existing robust RL algorithms offer a rich set of mechanisms and principles, yet two major barriers limit their broader potential: limited algorithm reusability and an unclear empirical capability boundary. We introduce RobustRLlib, an algorithm-centric library and benchmark that addresses both challenges. It integrates 17 representative robust online, offline, and safe RL algorithms under a unified interface for substantially improved reusability, together with an enhanced evaluation platform spanning diverse real-world shifts and advanced humanoid and vision-language-action tasks. Systematic evaluation over 273 perturbation configurations provides an up-to-date capability map of current robust RL algorithms, revealing where they remain effective and where substantial robustness gaps persist. As an open-source, user-friendly platform, RobustRLlib offers a reproducible and extensible codebase for applying existing methods to new problems and developing new robust RL algorithms.
ai_summary: Robust reinforcement learning (RL) is critical for reliable real-world deployment . Existing robust RL algorithms offer a rich set of mechanisms and principles, yet two major barriers limit their broader potential . RobustRLlib offers a reproducibibib, an algorithm-centric library and benchmark that addresses both challenges .

title: DexPort: A Hand-Held Skill Interface for Dexterous Hand Data Collection
abstract: Collecting high-quality demonstrations remains a central bottleneck for learning dexterous manipulation. Teleoperation records executable robot actions, but it requires a complete robot setup and places the burden of coordinating many finger joints on the operator. Human demonstrations are easier to collect, but their motions must be estimated and retargeted to the robot, and they do not directly provide robot actions. In this paper, we introduce DexPort, a portable data-collection interface for high-DoF robot hands. It uses the same hand hardware for collection and deployment, avoiding a hand embodiment gap, and records both commanded joint targets and measured joint states. Our key observation is that a small set of skills can support a wide range of dexterous tasks. During collection, the operator moves the hand-held interface to specify the robot wrist motion and selects or adjusts skills that coordinate the finger motion. This removes the need to control each joint independently while retaining behaviors such as precise grasping and in-hand manipulation. We collect demonstrations across several real-world tasks and in unstructured environments without a robot arm. We then use behavior cloning to train visuomotor policies directly on the recorded wrist motions and hand commands, without skill labels. We evaluate across 4 tasks: pick-and-place with diverse objects, screwing with in-hand tool use, drawer stowage which requires simultaneous grasp and pulling, and a bimanual scanning task. We collect over 2,500 demonstrations with our portable device, in both laboratory and in-the-wild settings. Across our tasks, we see an improvement from 11% to 64% when using recorded robot commands instead of states, and an improvement from 36% to 78% for task success when using in-the-wild data.
ai_summary: DexPort is a portable data-collection interface for high-DoF robot hands . It uses the same hand hardware for collection and deployment, avoiding a hand embodiment gap . It records both commanded joint targets and measured joint states .

title: SceneBloom: Agentic Indoor Environment Generation with Realistic and Diverse Layouts for Embodied Learning
abstract: Training generalizable embodied agents requires realistic, varied, and simulation-ready indoor environments. Language-guided methods support semantic planning and object-level reasoning, but precise spatial grounding remains difficult. Visual generative models offer rich priors over plausible arrangements, yet their outputs require geometric reasoning to become physically valid 3D scenes. We introduce SceneBloom, an agentic framework that combines visual layout sampling with contract-guided 3D compilation. A hierarchical sampler uses diffusion priors to generate furniture arrangements within functional zones. A compiler then uses relations extracted from each proposal to guide geometric fitting and local pose correction. Across five room types, SceneBloom attains the highest visual quality and physical stability among the compared methods and is the only method with no detected mesh collisions and out-of-bounds objects. Its layouts are also closer to the distribution of real rooms than those of all compared baselines. Object navigation policies trained in these realistic scenes achieve a higher success rate in held-out real scans than those trained on an equal number of real training scans. Code is available at https://github.com/Tinaliu0123/scenebloom.

title: The Language of Instruction: Genre and Generative AI
abstract: This article argues that instruction-fine-tuned language models should be understood as implementing a genre, what is proposed as the instructional-conversational genre. This genre is an amalgamation of discursive language from prior conversations between generative models and humans recursively run through these massive neural networks. It is instantiated in applications through instruction fine-tuning, the inclusion of a pretext known as a system prompt, and the formalization of inputs in mark-up languages characterized by the use of special tokens and role assignment in turntaking structures.
ai_summary: The genre is an amalgamation of discursive language from prior conversations between generative models and humans . It is instantiated in applications through instruction fine-tuning, the inclusion of a pretext known as a system prompt .

title: UniAction: Unified Action Conditioning for World Models
abstract: Actions that condition world models are highly heterogeneous, and thus existing action-conditioned world models are typically built for individual action types, fragmenting already limited action-annotated data across separate models. We introduce UniAction, a unified action-conditioning framework that represents any action as a sparse set of action elements, each with a discrete semantic identity and a continuous spatiotemporal grounding coordinate. By mapping these coordinates directly into the pretrained video model's native positional space, UniAction allows heterogeneous actions to condition a shared world model within the same spatiotemporal structure. We further introduce cardinality-calibrated attention to address the bias from differing action representation granularities. We evaluate UniAction on four representative action forms: force, camera control, hand pose, and robot pose. UniAction outperforms conditioning alternatives in action following, and a single jointly trained model surpasses the action-specific experts, showing that heterogeneous action data benefit from unified model and joint training.

title: MiD-VLM: Detecting and Grounding Global Semantic Misinformation in Image-Caption Pairs
abstract: Semantic misinformation can arise when an authentic image is paired with a caption that changes or distorts its narrative. Because the image itself may contain no visible signs of manipulation, methods designed to detect pixel-level artifacts can miss these misleading image-caption pairs. We study this problem using DGM4+, a dataset designed to evaluate the detection of global scene and semantic inconsistencies. We propose a multimodal model that combines image-text representations from SigLIP with visual scene features from DINOv2 through a projection MLP, and adapts Qwen2-VL-7B using LoRA. The model jointly predicts whether an image-caption pair is authentic, identifies the manipulation type, and grounds the misleading caption tokens. On the DGM4+ validation split, the model achieves an F1 score of $0.9679$ for binary authenticity classification. These results suggest that parameter-efficient adaptation of vision-language models is promising for detecting semantic inconsistencies, while also motivating further work on precise token-level grounding.
ai_summary: Semantic misinformation can arise when an authentic image is paired with a caption that changes or distorts its narrative . We study this problem using DGM4+ a dataset designed to evaluate the detection of global scene and semantic inconsistencies .

title: ViT-H: Generative Video-To-Humanoid Control with Motion Tracking Feedback
abstract: Learning humanoid control from monocular human videos offers a scalable way to acquire diverse whole-body behaviors. Yet, existing reconstruction-retargeting-tracking pipelines are limited in system-level scalability by separately optimized intermediate stages and cannot directly optimize reference motion executability using downstream tracking feedback. We present ViT-H, a video-to-humanoid control framework following a generation-and-tracking paradigm. ViT-H directly generates humanoid reference motions from videos with a diffusion model, bypassing human motion reconstruction and retargeting, and uses motion-tracking outcomes to post-train the generator with direct preference optimization. We further introduce an autoregressive variant that enables real-time humanoid video teleoperation with sub-400 ms latency. Extensive experiments on the Unitree G1 demonstrate that ViT-H outperforms state-of-the-art reconstruction-retargeting-tracking pipelines in both motion quality and executability. We further show that ViT-H scales favorably with model size and with both pre-training and post-training data scale, while motion-tracking feedback consistently improves executability across different motion trackers.
ai_summary: ViT-H is a video-to-humanoid control framework following a generation-and-tracking paradigm . It generates humanoid reference motions from videos with a diffusion model, bypassing human motion reconstruction and retargeting . It uses motion-tracking outcomes to post-train the generator with direct preference optimization .

title: Flownomaly: Single-Step Conditional-Mean Recovery for Few-Shot Anomaly Detection
abstract: Few-shot industrial anomaly detection requires modeling category-specific normality from only a handful of defect-free images. Common approaches tie inference to stored exemplars, impose rigid linear structure, or risk reproducing anomalous content. Flownomaly instead casts the problem as normal-counterpart recovery in frozen DINOv2 feature space. Given normal supports, a velocity field is learned through conditional flow matching over frozen patch tokens to transport Gaussian noise toward normal features. Along straight paths, a single recovery step using one evaluation of the optimal field yields the posterior mean of the clean normal token without trajectory integration. The operating time governs how strongly recovery modifies a query token. With no anomalous validation samples available for tuning, a normal-only Jacobian gain-to-noise criterion selects this time from the supports alone. Squared residuals between query tokens and their recovered counterparts yield anomaly signals for both dense localization and image-level detection. Across 1-, 2-, and 4-shot benchmarks on MVTec-AD and VisA, together with sample-shot evaluations on Real-IAD, Flownomaly achieves state-of-the-art performance against recent category-specific methods. In the 1-shot setting, image- and pixel-level AUROC reach 97.8% and 98.0% on MVTec-AD and 95.3% and 98.7% on VisA, with a 2.1-point image-level AUROC improvement over the strongest baseline on VisA. Code is available at https://github.com/b-rbmp/Flownomaly.
ai_summary: Few-shot industrial anomaly detection requires modeling category-specific normality from only a handful of defect-free images . Flownomaly instead casts the problem as normal-counterpart recovery in frozen DINOv2 feature space .

title: Measure Before You Train: Typed Decision Models vs. a Classical Baseline vs. a Generative LLM for Routing a Personal Multilingual Inbox
abstract: Personal email agents decide, for every message, what it is, whether it is urgent, whether to draft a reply, create a task, or ignore it. Their error rate is rarely measured: the stored labels were written by the system itself. We present Foyer, a self-hosted personal inbox agent in daily use, and a measurement protocol (stratified sampling, frozen snapshots, thread-grouped splits, pre-registered hypotheses, human labels in the agent's review loop) that yields ground truth before any training. On 739 real Italian/English emails labelled by the owner (231 unbiased, 500 adversarially sampled), we compare nine systems under thread-grouped cross-validation: the production keyword rules, a TF-IDF + logistic-regression baseline, local typed decision models (Tev1, Nimble), a hosted decision model (Nimble v4-max), and hosted generative LLMs (Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma 4 26B/31B). Four results. The production rules score 28% on message type against a 58% majority class: the field shown most prominently carried no information. With ~200 labels, logistic regression has the highest accuracy on every field (type 0.79, urgency 0.74, needs-reply 0.83, is-noise 0.90), though it never predicts the two rarest classes and is statistically tied with Gemma 4 on type; few-shot prompting does not close the gap. The sender's relationship (client, supplier, service) is recovered from other emails of the same contact with 98.6% accuracy where the contact has been seen, and is not inferable from a single message by any model: it belongs in the contact graph, not the prompt. Finally, accuracy is not the product metric: composed into actions, the most accurate system most often ignores emails needing action (18% vs 4% for the best LLM); a cost-chosen threshold on its noise probability halves that rate and makes it the cheapest system.
ai_summary: Foyer is a self-hosted personal inbox agent in daily use . Foyer uses a measurement protocol that yields ground truth before any training . The production rules score 28% on message type against a 58% majority class .

title: Where Rounding Happens Matters: Rounding-Location Alignment Stabilizes LLM Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Reinforcement learning for large language models often uses separate systems for inference and training. Even with identical weights and BF16 tensors, implementation differences can make an intended on-policy update off-policy and destabilize training. Existing remedies align the entire inference and training stacks, change global precision, or modify the learning algorithm. We ask whether aligning selected parts of the execution stack can stabilize BF16 RL while other implementation differences remain. We align training-side rounding locations with inference in three regions---RoPE, SwiGLU, and residual RMSNorm---by retaining selected intermediates in FP32 until their BF16 outputs. Across four Qwen-family models, aligning all three regions prevents the collapse observed under the default BF16 baseline; RoPE-path alignment alone also suffices in the studied runs, despite remaining numerical discrepancies. The interventions keep the inference engine, matrix-multiplication and attention kernels, and learning objective unchanged.
ai_summary: The Qwen-family models are based on different systems for inference and training . They use separate systems for training and inference, but implementation differences can make an intended on-policy update off-policy changes .

title: Beyond Discrete Tokens: Preserving Numerical Continuity in Medical Vision-Language Models
abstract: Objective: To develop a unified vision-language model for prompt-conditioned quantitative ultrasound measurement that addresses the mismatch between continuous measurement targets and discrete token-based numerical prediction. Methods: This article presents HAD-VLM, a hybrid autoregressive-diffusion framework that combines autoregressive text generation with continuous measurement prediction within a shared backbone. Visual prompt tuning adapts the vision encoder to ultrasound images. A diffusion process predicts a five-component representation comprising caliper endpoint coordinates and measurement length. A post-processing strategy combining the proposed coordinate-length consistency mechanism with ensemble prediction is introduced to refine measurement estimates. We evaluate four echocardiographic measurement tasks on EchoNet-LVH, with additional assessments of medical question answering and X-ray vertebral measurement. Results: HAD-VLM achieves mean absolute errors of 1.36, 2.77, 3.05, and 1.16 mm for IVSd, LVIDd, LVIDs, and LVPWd, respectively, reducing errors by 21.4-37.6\% relative to the Vicuna-based autoregressive baseline. It also outperforms fine-tuned Qwen3-VL and direct MLP regression across all four tasks. Medical question answering performance is preserved on the evaluated dataset. For X-ray vertebral measurement, HAD-VLM reduces mean absolute error from 11.4 to 6.7 pixels. Conclusion: Integrating autoregressive language generation with diffusion-based continuous prediction improves quantitative medical image measurement while retaining prompt-conditioned task flexibility. Significance: HAD-VLM provides a unified approach to combining language interaction with anatomically grounded numerical prediction for quantitative medical image analysis.
ai_summary: HAD-VLM is a hybrid autoregressive-diffusion framework that combines autore progressive text generation with continuous measurement prediction within a shared backbone . Visual prompt tuning adapts the vision encoder to ultrasound images .

title: Monetizing Intelligence: Advertising and Subscription Design on LLM Platforms
abstract: Large language model (LLM) platforms introducing advertising must decide how much capability ad revenue should fund and what consumers should pay to avoid ads. We study a monopolistic platform that jointly chooses costly response quality, advertising intensity, and subscription prices when advertising reduces user value but better service raises advertising returns. Three findings follow. First, when partly ad-supported and ad-free plans coexist, advertising can finance useful service for consumers who receive none under pure subscription. Lower effective quality in middle plans weakens the alternatives available to premium users, allowing higher prices for unchanged ad-free service. Some fully ad-supported users gain utility, while partly ad-supported and ad-free users lose: broader access can coexist with utility polarization. Second, an intermediate advertising cap can maximize consumer surplus by preserving some revenue that finances service while limiting degradation. Third, cheaper compute can raise quality and reduce ad intensity, yet sufficiently large cost reductions can increase aggregate advertising revenue above its initial level because better service raises the value of the remaining advertised interactions. An extension shows how advertising-funded upgrades can bring plans to the same maximum capability and advertising exposure, eliminating the basis for different prices. These results make menu design central to evaluating LLM advertising: the consequences extend beyond users who see ads to the alternatives and prices faced by those who do not.
ai_summary: Large language model (LLM) platforms must decide how much capability ad revenue should fund and what consumers should pay to avoid ads . We study a monopolistic platform that jointly chooses costly response quality, advertising intensity, and subscription prices .

title: Knowledge Distillation across Item and Code Spaces for Parallel Generative Recommendation
abstract: Generative recommendation with semantic IDs represents each item as a sequence of discrete codes derived from its semantic representation and predicts these codes to generate recommendations. Existing semantic-ID recommenders are typically trained with hard labels for the observed next item. Although such supervision identifies the target, it provides no explicit distributional information about alternative items conditioned on the same user history. Sequential recommenders can supply this item-level predictive knowledge, but transferring it to semantic-ID generation is challenging because the teacher and student operate in item and code spaces, respectively. We propose two complementary knowledge-distillation objectives for parallel semantic-ID recommenders, which predict all code positions simultaneously without autoregressive prefix conditioning. Item Distribution Matching (IDM) reconstructs a catalogue-level item distribution from the student's parallel code predictions and aligns it with the teacher's item distribution. Code Marginal Matching (CMM) projects the teacher's item probabilities onto each code position using fixed item-to-code assignments, then matches the resulting code marginals to the corresponding student heads. Both objectives transfer the teacher's soft distributional knowledge while preserving the student's parallel prediction structure. Experiments on benchmark datasets show that both methods consistently outperform existing state-of-the-art approaches. On average, IDM improves Recall@10 by 15.39%, while CMM improves NDCG@10 by 8.28%. These results demonstrate that distillation in either reconstructed item space or code-marginal space can substantially strengthen hard-label supervision for parallel generative recommendation.
ai_summary: Generative recommendation with semantic IDs represents each item as a sequence of discrete codes derived from its semantic representation . Existing semantic-ID recommenders are typically trained with hard labels for the observed next item .

title: If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models perform well on robotic manipulation, yet remain brittle once their own actions carry them into states their training data barely covers. Recovering from such failures usually requires recovery demonstrations, policy retraining, or a separate model at inference time. We introduce Backtrack, a lightweight failure detection and recovery mechanism for frozen VLAs that needs none of these. A small failure prediction head, trained only on outcome-labeled rollouts of the frozen policy, reads the VLA's existing internal representations to estimate whether the current episode will fail. When the predicted failure probability exceeds a threshold, a controller pauses the policy, retraces the arm's recently achieved motion, and hands control back to the unchanged policy so it can retry from an earlier configuration. The head adds only 0.48-0.88% to the policy's parameter count. We evaluate Backtrack on LIBERO with three VLAs spanning two action-generation families: SmolVLA and $π$0.5, which use flow-matching action experts, and the autoregressive $π$0-FAST. On LIBERO-Long, the suite of long-horizon multi-step tasks and the one on which all three policies fail most often, Backtrack reduces each policy's failure rate by 19-48%, raising success by up to 7.4 percentage points; on the three shorter suites, where control success is already 85-99%, its effect is smaller. On MetaWorld, all twelve controller configurations tested with SmolVLA improve on the unassisted policy.
ai_summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models perform well on robotic manipulation, but remain brittle once their own actions carry them into states their training data barely covers . Backtrack is a lightweight failure detection and recovery mechanism for frozen VLAs that needs none of these.

title: Learning Positive Linear Combinations of ReLUs in Fully Polynomial Time
abstract: We study the fundamental problem of PAC learning positive linear combinations of $k$ arbitrary ReLU activations on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with respect to the Gaussian distribution, in $L_2$ loss. We give the first fully-polynomial time algorithm for this learning task. Specifically, our algorithm draws $\mathrm{poly}(d, k, 1/ε)$ samples, runs in $\mathrm{poly}(d, k, 1/ε)$ time, and outputs a hypothesis that is $ε$-close to the target concept with high probability. All prior algorithms for this problem require super-polynomial time in $k$ or $1/ε$, or leverage strong well-conditioned assumptions on the weight matrix. On a technical level, our approach develops a novel boosting procedure of a ``weak'' learner that recovers the hidden weight vectors to constant error, in a list-decodable manner. To develop this ``weak'' learning procedure, we leverage implicit tensor computation techniques to construct a low-degree filtering procedure based on Hermite tensors of the target function. This procedure amplifies separation among (clusters of) weight vectors to learn each of them to constant error. We then argue that the same procedure can be used for improving the estimation of hidden weight vectors, using gradient descent-like updates on the Euclidean sphere. A crucial ingredient of our algorithm is a pruning approach that ensures only relevant vectors that approximate the hidden weight vectors at target accuracy are maintained by the algorithm.

title: Runtime BiDi Structural Verification Catches Right-to-Left Layout Defects that Accessibility, Actionability, and Logical-Property Linting Miss
abstract: Bidirectional (right-to-left, RTL) layout defects arise when interfaces authored with physical directional CSS (margin-left, border-left, text-align:left) are rendered under dir="rtl" without being mirrored. Accessibility engines (axe-core), actionability engines (Playwright), and even Stylelint's current core logical-property rule fail to localise these defects. We present runtime structural invariants -- a zero-golden mode over computed style and geometry, and a bidi-conservative differential mode -- that catch them in a headless browser. On a held-out benchmark of 14 real RTL bugs reconstructed from dated fix commits in Bootstrap and Material Components Web, the detector recovers 13/14 (2 via zero-golden, 11 via the differential mode), with no false alarm on any patched version; on the actual committed historical bootstrap.rtl.css it catches 1 of 2 attempted. It reports 0 false positives on 16 negative LTR-island cases and, in both modes, on 43 unmodified real components across four design systems and three RTL architectures (rule-of-three 95% upper bound <= 7%), and it surfaced a real directional defect in the current Bulma 1.0.4. By contrast, Stylelint's core rule emits an identical 1744 warnings on Bootstrap's LTR and correct-RTL builds, pseudo-localisation detects none of the mirroring bugs, and a naive pixel mirror-and-diff reaches only F1 0.87 with a test-set-tuned threshold. The two modes are complementary: zero-golden is the sole detector of the decoration/styling-asymmetry class (5/6) but false-flags the correct logical border-inline-end, while the differential detects none of that class yet never false-alarms and is empirically exact on the block-level inset/margin class. We scope this paper to detection; repair is future work.
ai_summary: Bidirectional layout defects arise when interfaces authored with physical directional CSS are rendered under dir="rtl" without being mirrored . Accessibility engines (axe-core), actionability engines (Playwright) and even Stylelint's current logical-property rule fail to localise these defects .

title: Yalda-Embedding: Open Development of a Competitive Persian Retrieval Model
abstract: Despite advances in multilingual text representations, effective dense retrieval for Persian remains constrained by the limited availability of language-specific training resources and compact embedding models. We present Yalda Embedding, a 595.8-million-parameter Persian retrieval model adapted from Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B using more than one million query-document pairs. On eight Persian retrieval tasks from FaMTEB, the model achieves the highest macro-average among the evaluated 0.6B models, scoring 0.5488 and outperforming Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B and F2LLM-v2-0.6B on every task. It also approaches Qwen3-Embedding-4B, winning on four tasks, tying on one, and trailing by 0.0075 in macro-average. An incremental ablation study examines contrastive batch size, optimization stabilization, and relational knowledge distillation from F2LLM-v2-8B. Under the one-epoch training setup, contrastive fine-tuning alone yields a modest mean improvement over initialization and regressions on two tasks. The final distilled configuration improves all eight tasks over the non-distilled model, raising the mean from 0.4813 to 0.5488 without increasing inference-time model size. These gains include hard-negative evaluation tasks despite training without explicitly mined or supplied hard negatives. We release model weights, training and evaluation code, the pairwise dataset, and its teacher-embedded counterpart, enabling inspection of data composition and training procedures, independent evaluation, and reuse without repeating expensive teacher inference.

title: STROKE: Simple Sparse Structural Occlusions for Black-Box Adversarial Attacks
abstract: We introduce STROKE, a query-efficient score-based black-box adversarial attack that constructs perturbations from simple oriented rectangular occlusions. STROKE optimizes these perturbations through a lightweight greedy add-and-refine procedure. Across diverse image classifiers, STROKE achieves high attack success with low query counts at nominal 1--2\% area settings, showing favorable performance relative to existing patch-based attacks in several configurations. Matched comparisons further demonstrate substantial reductions in wall-clock attack time, while ablation studies examine the key design choices and effectiveness across structural primitives. These findings suggest that simple structural occlusions offer an effective and computationally efficient search space for black-box adversarial attacks.
ai_summary: STROKE optimizes these perturbations through a lightweight greedy add-and-refine procedure . STROke achieves high attack success with low query counts at nominal 1--2\% area settings .

title: ZENO: Nonlinear filtering with Zakai Equation Neural Operators
abstract: State inference and parameter learning for nonlinear filters is a core computation for scientific machine learning with varied applications in engineering and neuroscience. The unnormalized filtering distribution is governed by the Zakai equation, a stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE) that combines the forward Kolmogorov operator (known as the Fokker-Planck equation) with observed likelihood updates. Although solving these high-dimensional SPDEs is often impossible analytically and intractable numerically, advances in operator learning and physics-informed machine learning have made it feasible. Harnessing these advances, we introduce the Zakai Equation Neural Operator (ZENO), a model that optimizes a neural operator against a Zakai Equation based physics-informed loss to approximate the exact unnormalized filtering distribution for latent stochastic dynamical systems. We use this ZENO-inferred posterior distribution in an expectation-maximization (EM) framework to perform parameter learning and state inference. We demonstrate ZENO's ability to accurately infer the posterior distribution and learn its corresponding SDE parameters in three simulated stochastic dynamical systems (Double-Well bistable system, Van Der Pol (VDP) oscillator, and Lorenz system) and compare its performance against established methods for latent SDE inference and learning. We show that ZENO recovers previously observed limit cycles representing forward and backward locomotion from a whole-brain imaging dataset of immobilized \textit{C. elegans} nematodes. ZENO is a novel approach to the problem of nonlinear filtering and dynamical inference through the lens of partial differential equations and operator theory.
ai_summary: Unnormalized filtering distribution is governed by the Zakai equation . The Zakai Equation Neural Operator (ZENO) is a model that optimizes a neural operator against a ZENO-based loss .

title: On the Expressive Power of Hook-Indexed State Comprehending State in the React UI Library
abstract: React is currently the most popular JavaScript library for front-end web development. It endows UI components with state via the useState construct, through a mechanism that we name hook-indexed state. However, React's implementation of hook-indexed state is both fragile and poorly understood. Programmers frequently experience unexpected behavior, and the benefits of programming in this paradigm are wholly unclear. We define Lambda-React-Hook, a core calculus that captures the essence of hook-indexed state, and give it a type system to statically rule out unexpected behavior. We then translate Lambda-React-Hook into a calculus Lambda-React-Ref based on ML-style references, and prove that this translation preserves typability and semantics, thus showing that hook-indexed state is expressible in terms of standard references. The translation is local and admits a compositional definition, but involves significant code duplication. As well as illuminating the essence of state in React, our observations can inform the design of future reactive programming systems.

title: Adaptive Frequency Threshold Byte Pair Encoding for Mixed Natural Language and Structured Symbolic Corpora
abstract: Modern language models rely on subwording tokenization to define the discrete units of input processing, typically using methods like Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) that treat whitespace as a fixed semantic boundary. This design is inherently limited, as many meaningful concepts---including multiword expressions and the structured environments of formal languages like LaTeX---frequently span across whitespaces. While recent superword tokenization methods attempt to address this by relaxing whitespace constraints, they often rely on greedy frequency-driven merging that fails to account for token length or the specific needs of underrepresented domain-specific languages. In this paper, we introduce Adaptive Frequency Threshold Byte Pair Encoding (AdaBPE), a new tokenization method that leverages an adaptive frequent-pattern mining approach. AdaBPE features a twofold dynamicity: it adapts minimum frequency thresholds based on both the length of a candidate token, to prevent favoring frequent short patterns, and its type, to distinguish between general and formal language patterns, using LaTeX as case in point. This allows the model to efficiently allocate vocabulary capacity to domain-specific notations, such as LaTeX, even when they represent a small fraction of the training data. We evaluate AdaBPE across five datasets spanning LaTeX and natural language, showing consistent gains in encoding efficiency and downstream language-model performance on domain-specific content without compromising general-language performance.

title: SemantEq: Faithful Bidirectional Equivalence of Formal Statements
abstract: Statement autoformalization translates mathematics from natural language into a proof assistant such as Lean 4, and models now do it at scale. As provers get stronger, the burden of correctness shifts from the proof to the statement, that is, to whether the formal statement faithfully translates its source. Given a trusted reference formalization, the natural test is logical equivalence, and it proves too much. $P \leftrightarrow Q$ holds trivially for any two statements $P$ and $Q$ that the library proves, because a prover can prove each separately and pass through $P \leftrightarrow \mathrm{True} \leftrightarrow Q$. The stronger the prover, the more unrelated pairs pass. Earlier methods restrict the prover and check that each proof names the other statement. We introduce SemantEq, a more principled relation that instead requires each statement to turn into the other only through a chain of allowed steps, such as logical rearrangement and rewriting with the library's own equations. Our programs judge a proof by the proof term Lean checks, not by its tactic script. SemantEq-Eval, a search without a model, reaches 100% precision and 65.6% recall on the ProofNetVerif test split under our adjudicated labels, against 95.8% and 61.8% for BEq+, and an 8.9-fold increase in its CPU time adds at most three pairs. A language model finds more proofs, but under two of four prompts it proves both directions of about two in five of the non-equivalent pairs. SemantEq-ProofAudit audits each model-written proof under a policy derived from the relation and accepts none of the 104 non-equivalent pairs, and it raises recall on 407 equivalent pairs from 65.4% to 81.1% under the best prompt. Separating the generation of equivalence proofs from their acceptance lets a stronger prover raise recall without changing what an acceptance means. We release code and data at: https://github.com/hlxr89/SemantEq

title: A Tutorial on Physics Constrained Machine Learning for Hybrid Modeling, Optimization, and Control
abstract: Physics-constrained machine learning (PCML) integrates domain knowledge, first-principles, and physical constraints into AI/ML models. In this work, we present a step-by-step tutorial of a modular PCML framework, KKT-HardNet, and illustrate how it could be used for hybrid modeling, process simulation, optimization and model predictive control in a single platform. KKT-HardNet combines fast inference capabilities of neural networks with guaranteed satisfaction of algebraic constraints through differential projection. It can handle heterogeneous data and enforce both linear and nonlinear equality and inequality constraints. The modular design supports custom neural-network backbones and user-defined projection mechanisms for PCML. To enable efficient end-to-end training, KKT-HardNet exploits implicit function theorem to backpropagate through the projection layer. This avoids computationally expensive automatic differentiation. This work also introduces an exact reduced-order Fischer-Burmeister reformulation and a primal-dual interior-point method as an alternative projection solve strategy. We also provide a diverse set of benchmarking problems for PCML in engineering applications. KKT-HardNet achieves orders of magnitude better performance in terms of both constraint satisfaction and inference time. The KKT-HardNet code and the benchmark datasets are available at https://github.com/souls-tamu/kkt-hardnet .

It can handle heterogeneous data and enforce both linear and nonlinear equality and inequality constraints . The modular design supports custom neural-network backbones and user-defined projection mechanisms for PCML .

title: Recommender regret for improving regularised RL estimation with bandits and MCTS
abstract: Regularised reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms rely on estimators, like Monte Carlo tree search or one-step look-ahead, to provide policy, value, or Q-value estimates in training and inference. However, existing bandit-based estimation frameworks evaluate sampling efficiency, not the quality of estimates. We address this by formalising estimate generation as a recommendation process, treating bandit-based sampling as an improvement operator. To evaluate the quality of a recommendation (estimate), we define regulariser-aware recommender regrets, analysing their lower bounds, and proving that simple algorithms like uniform sampling can achieve these bounds. Finally, we unify bandit- and search-based target improvement under recommender MCTS. Across synthetic trees, arcade games, and scientific discovery tasks, recommenders often yield faster target convergence and superior downstream performance. Our experiments characterise for the first time the potential of regularised MCTS in scientific applications.
ai_summary: Regularised reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms rely on estimators to provide policy, value, or Q-value estimates in training and inference . But existing bandit-based estimation frameworks evaluate sampling efficiency, not the quality of estimates . We address this by formalising estimate generation as a recommendation process .

title: EVSEFuzz : A Tool for Automated Testing of Protocol Implementations
abstract: The rapid adoption and development of electric vehicle (EV) networks has required the expansive deployment of EV charging infrastructure (EVCI) which relies on communication protocols such as the open charge point protocol (OCPP) to coordinate data transfer between charging network operators and the EV supply equipment. In this paper, we present EVSEFuzz, a tool for automatically building fuzzers to test the security of protocol implementations. To achieve this we make a novel use of Python datatype validation packages and tools to ``understand'' datatypes and message structures and generate both compliant and non-compliant messages. To date, EVSEFuzz has been tested successfully with several open and closed-source implementations and has found several vulnerabilities leading to the publication of two CVEs.
ai_summary: EVSEFuzz is a tool for automatically building fuzzers to test the security of protocol implementations . It uses Python datatype validation packages and tools to "understand'' datatypes and message structures and generate both compliant and non-compliant messages .

title: LoCA: Enabling Multi-Modality in Geospatial Location Encoders
abstract: Location encoders map geographic coordinates to high-dimensional descriptors through contrastive alignment with paired Earth Observation imagery. We prove that this construction is structurally limited: any Lipschitz location encoder produces an output of intrinsic dimension at most 2, regardless of architecture or bandwidth, which forces the contrastive loss to strictly exceed its asymptotic optimum. Empirically, joint training also collapses the encoder's embedding covariance to low rank. Although dimension-limited, current location encoders sidestep this spectral collapse by training against a frozen image encoder, which we reinterpret as a covariance regularizer that supplies a high-rank target for the location encoder to fold onto. However, extending this approach to multimodal inputs is challenging, as location encoders should simultaneously map a single location to multiple, potentially incompatible, descriptors. We identify two requirements a regularizer must satisfy for location encoding in multimodal regimes: co-alignment across modalities, since adapters alone cannot align independently pretrained encoders; and high effective rank, since the location encoder inherits its target's spectrum. We propose LoCA (Location Contrastive Alignment), a two-stage pipeline that satisfies both. Stage 1 jointly trains Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 encoders with contrastive learning, producing a co-aligned, high-rank multimodal target. Stage 2 freezes the image encoders and trains a location and a tabular metadata encoder as projection adapters with multi-view contrastive learning. Against five state-of-the-art encoders on 17 tasks ranging from land cover and wildfire forecasting to geophysical, socio-economic, biodiversity and climate applications, LoCA achieves the most task wins, is the only model to outperform every other on a majority of tasks, and wins 68.8% of all per-task comparisons.

title: Green Code or Costly Code? Evaluating the Energy Costs of Iterative LLM-Based Code Optimizations
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used to optimize code for performance. This practice often assumes that improvements in execution speed naturally translate into overall lower energy consumption. We challenge this assumption empirically by measuring whether performance-optimized code produced by LLM self-refinement pipelines is also energy-efficient relative to canonical human reference solutions, and whether the energy cost of the optimization process can be offset by subsequent execution-time savings. We evaluate 11 open-source models across four decoding configurations on all 1,000 problems of EffiBench, a state-of-the-art performance benchmark, while collecting per-process, hardware-level energy measurements throughout. Inference energy spans 0.79 to 8.68 MJ across model-variant pairs, which is roughly equivalent to the energy of 250 to 2800 GPT-4.1 queries. Limiting the maximum number of output tokens has the largest impact, reducing energy use by up to 69% compared to the default configuration. On the execution side, 42 of 44 configurations produce code that consumes more energy per problem than the canonical human reference, with overheads ranging from +4% to +886%. The two exceptions achieve only marginal gains, with break-even points on the order of 10^6 to 10^7 executions. Mixture-of-Experts architectures consume substantially less inference energy than equivalently-sized dense models without sacrificing correctness, making architectural choice a more consequential sustainability lever than decoding parameters. Performance optimization and energy efficiency are not always aligned goals: LLM self-refinement consistently produces faster-seeking but energy-heavier code relative to what a human engineer would write. All artifacts are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23598170.

This practice often assumes that improvements in execution speed naturally translate into lower energy consumption . We challenge this assumption by measuring whether performance-optimized code produced by LLM self-refinement pipelines is also energy-efficient .

title: Closing the Modality Gap via Simplex-Constrained Representations
abstract: While multimodal contrastive models like CLIP and CLAP successfully learn shared representations, their embeddings typically exhibit a persistent \emph{modality gap}. We propose addressing this separation through a purely geometric approach: changing the embedding domain from the unit sphere, $S^{d-1}$, to the probability simplex, $Δ^{d-1}$. Although both manifolds share the same intrinsic dimension, the simplex acts as a structural prior; its nonnegative, unit-mass constraints serve as a cross-modal calibration that forces both modalities to ground themselves in the same coordinate system. By attaching lightweight softmax adapters and using Total Variation similarity, we reduce the centroid $\ell_2$ gap by 97--99\% across five multimodal retrieval benchmarks. This confirms that simplicial geometry induces genuine semantic alignment, matching or exceeding the retrieval performance of standard unconstrained models.

title: When Human Corrections Travel: Safety in Federated VLA Adaptation
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies can adapt to local human intervention, while federated learning can combine distributed robot experience without pooling raw records. We examine their prospective intersection: sharing adaptations derived from diverse human corrections across tasks, environments, people, and robot embodiments. Corrections differ in modality, safety semantics(urgency, behavioral scope, etc.), and privacy sensitivity. A shared update that improves mean task success may suppress a rare safety intervention or produce an unsafe response on another robot. We argue for three requirements: preserve the context and uncertainty of multimodal corrections when deciding what to share; assess candidate updates in each receiving robot's closed loop before deployment; and evaluate leakage alongside retention of safety-critical evidence. Immediate, legible defensive behavior remains necessary during human interaction. We offer counterexamples and a falsifiable evaluation agenda, not experimental results.
